newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN AVERAGE LENDING RATE RISES TO 10.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN AVERAGE LENDING RATE RISES TO 10.3 PCT.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate jumped to 10.3 percent on Monday from 7.8 percent on increased demand by banks.
But individual rates were unchanged despite shrinking supply, particularly of term funds.
Roughly half the 69.3 million kuna settlements were new call money placements at a steady 7.0 percent.
Lenders also rolled over almost 34 million kuna in old term loans at rates ranging between 7.0 percent for one-week and 15 percent for two-month interbank money.
Savings banks were charged slightly higher prices.
Demand rose after the state pension fund began paying July pensions today, straining banking sector liquidity.

The central bank said it would decide whether or not to intervene in order to help banks on Tuesday after getting a report on their overnight balances and pay orders for the next few days from the central payments agency ZAP.
It can buy hard currency surpluses from banks, or repurchase outstanding liquidity or T-bills, injecting kuna for either operation two days later.

The bank calculated the kuna midrates for Tuesday stronger at 6.6007 versus 6.6517 against the dollar but a touch weaker at 3.5539 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
